There is currently a great deal of interest in the theoretical and practical possibility of cloaking objects from the observation by electromagnetic waves. The basic idea of these invisibility devices \cite{glu1, glu2, le},\cite{pss1} is to use anisotropic {\it transformation media} whose permittivity and permeability $\var^{\lambda
u}, \mu^{\lambda
u}$, are obtained from the ones, $\var_0^{\lambda
u}, \mu^{\lambda
u}_0$, of isotropic media, by singular transformations of coordinates. In this paper we study electromagnetic cloaking in the time-domain using the formalism of time-dependent scattering theory. This formalism allows us to settle in an unambiguous way the mathematical problems posed by the singularities of the inverse of the permittivity and the permeability of the {\it transformation media} on the boundary of the cloaked objects. We write Maxwell's equations in Schr"odinger form with the electromagnetic propagator playing the role of the Hamiltonian. We prove that the electromagnetic propagator outside of the cloaked objects is essentially self-adjoint. Moreover, the unique self-adjoint extension is unitarily equivalent to the electromagnetic propagator in the medium $\var_0^{\lambda
u}, \mu^{\lambda
u}_0$. Using this fact, and since the coordinate transformation is the identity outside of a ball, we prove that the scattering operator is the identity. Our results give a rigorous proof that the construction of \cite{glu1, glu2, le}, \cite{pss1} perfectly cloaks passive and active devices from observation by electromagnetic waves. Furthermore, we prove cloaking for general anisotropic materials. In particular, our results prove that it is possible to cloak objects inside general crystals.

outputs.L1:
There is currently considerable interest in the theoretical and practical feasibility of cloaking objects from observation by electromagnetic waves. The fundamental idea underlying these invisibility devices \cite{glu1, glu2, le, pss1} is to employ anisotropic {\it transformation media} whose permittivity and permeability, $\var^{\lambda
u}$ and $\mu^{\lambda
u}$, are obtained from those of isotropic media, $\var_0^{\lambda
u}$ and $\mu_0^{\lambda
u}$, through singular coordinate transformations. In this paper, we study electromagnetic cloaking in the time domain using the formalism of time-dependent scattering theory. This framework enables us to resolve unambiguously the mathematical problems arising from singularities in the inverses of the permittivity and permeability of the {\it transformation media} at the boundaries of the cloaked objects. We express Maxwell's equations in Schr"odinger form, with the electromagnetic propagator playing the role of the Hamiltonian, and prove that the electromagnetic propagator outside the cloaked objects is essentially self-adjoint. Moreover, its unique self-adjoint extension is unitarily equivalent to the electromagnetic propagator in the medium characterized by $\var_0^{\lambda
u}$ and $\mu_0^{\lambda
u}$. Using this equivalence, together with the fact that the coordinate transformation is the identity outside a ball, we prove that the scattering operator is the identity. Our results provide a rigorous proof that the constructions of \cite{glu1, glu2, le, pss1} perfectly cloak both passive and active devices from observation by electromagnetic waves. Furthermore, we establish cloaking for general anisotropic materials. In particular, our results demonstrate that objects can be cloaked within general crystals.
outputs.L2:
Electromagnetic invisibility cloaks have attracted substantial attention, both as theoretical constructs and as potentially realizable devices. The approach introduced in \cite{glu1, glu2, le}, \cite{pss1} relies on anisotropic *transformation media*. Their permittivity and permeability tensors, $\var^{\lambda\nu}$ and $\mu^{\lambda\nu}$, are generated from the corresponding tensors $\var_0^{\lambda\nu}$ and $\mu_0^{\lambda\nu}$ of isotropic materials through singular coordinate transformations.

Here, electromagnetic cloaking is analyzed in the time domain within the framework of time-dependent scattering theory. This method provides a mathematically precise treatment of the singular behavior exhibited by the inverses of the transformation medium’s permittivity and permeability at the surface of the concealed region. Maxwell’s equations are recast in Schrödinger form, with the electromagnetic propagator taking the place of the Hamiltonian.

We establish that the propagator governing the electromagnetic field outside the hidden objects is essentially self-adjoint. Its sole self-adjoint extension is also shown to be unitarily equivalent to the electromagnetic propagator associated with the original medium characterized by $\var_0^{\lambda\nu}$ and $\mu_0^{\lambda\nu}$. Because the underlying coordinate map coincides with the identity beyond a ball, this equivalence implies that the scattering operator itself is the identity.

These conclusions rigorously demonstrate that the constructions proposed in \cite{glu1, glu2, le}, \cite{pss1} achieve perfect electromagnetic concealment for both passive objects and active devices. The analysis additionally extends cloaking to arbitrary anisotropic materials, showing in particular that objects can be hidden within general crystalline media.
outputs.L3:
Electromagnetic cloaking relies on anisotropic transformation media whose permittivity and permeability tensors are obtained from those of an isotropic background medium through singular coordinate transformations. These transformations guide electromagnetic fields around a designated region, effectively isolating its contents from external observation. However, the resulting material parameters become singular at the boundary of the cloaked region, creating significant mathematical challenges.

The paper addresses these difficulties by analyzing cloaking in the time domain within a rigorous scattering-theory framework. Maxwell’s equations are recast in Schrödinger form, allowing electromagnetic evolution to be described by a propagator. The authors show that the propagator governing fields outside the cloaked objects is essentially self-adjoint despite the singular behavior of the transformation medium. Consequently, it admits a unique self-adjoint extension, ensuring well-defined electromagnetic time evolution without the need for arbitrary boundary conditions at the cloaking interface.

This unique extension is then shown to be unitarily equivalent to the propagator associated with the original, uncloaked medium. As a result, the corresponding scattering operator is the identity: incoming electromagnetic waves emerge without any detectable alteration attributable to the cloak or the object concealed within it. Thus, no scattered field reveals the presence of the cloaked region.

These results provide a rigorous mathematical foundation for perfect electromagnetic cloaking in the time domain. They apply both to passive objects and to active devices located inside the cloaked region, and they remain valid for broad classes of anisotropic background materials. In particular, the theory encompasses cloaked objects embedded in crystalline media, substantially extending the scope of transformation-based cloaking beyond simple isotropic environments.
outputs.L4:
The paper develops a rigorous scattering-theoretic analysis of electromagnetic cloaking in the time domain. The cloaks are constructed by transformation optics: a singular change of spatial variables expands a point, curve, or lower-dimensional set into a finite region that contains the object to be hidden. Applying this transformation to the original permittivity and permeability tensors produces anisotropic material parameters that become singular or degenerate at the cloaking interface. Because of this singular behavior, the usual formulations of Maxwell’s equations and their standard boundary conditions cannot be applied without additional functional-analytic justification.

To address the problem, Maxwell’s equations are rewritten as a Schrödinger-type evolution equation,
\[
i\partial_t \Psi=A\Psi,
\]
where \(\Psi\) contains the electric and magnetic fields and \(A\) is the Maxwell generator. The natural state space is a weighted Hilbert space defined by the electromagnetic energy, with weights determined by the permittivity and permeability tensors. This formulation makes it possible to define finite-energy fields even when the constitutive parameters are singular at the boundary of the cloaked region.

The principal mathematical result is that the exterior Maxwell generator is essentially self-adjoint on smooth fields supported away from the cloaking interface. Consequently, it has a unique self-adjoint extension and generates a well-defined unitary time evolution. No arbitrary boundary condition needs to be imposed from the exterior: the physically relevant behavior at the singular interface is already fixed by finite energy and self-adjointness.

The exterior propagator is then shown to be unitarily equivalent to the Maxwell propagator in the original, uncloaked medium. The unitary transformation is induced by the singular coordinate map used to construct the cloak. Thus, although the transformed fields and material tensors can be highly singular near the cloaking boundary, exterior electromagnetic evolution is equivalent to free evolution—or, more generally, to evolution in the original background medium.

This equivalence yields a particularly strong scattering result. The wave operators exist and, under the natural identification of the original and transformed energy spaces, the electromagnetic scattering operator is the identity. An incoming finite-energy wave therefore produces exactly the same asymptotic exterior field as it would in the absence of both the cloak and the hidden object. There is no reflected or scattered component that could reveal the cloaked region. The conclusion holds in the full time domain rather than only for individual frequencies, establishing perfect dynamical cloaking.

The analysis also clarifies the relation between the exterior and interior fields. The singular interface decouples the finite-energy exterior dynamics from the evolution inside the cloaked region. Accordingly, arbitrary passive objects can be placed inside without altering exterior measurements. Active devices and sources may also be concealed, provided that the interior fields and sources satisfy the compatibility conditions associated with the interior Maxwell operator and its admissible boundary behavior. Under these conditions, radiation generated inside cannot propagate into the exterior.

Importantly, the argument does not depend on an isotropic or homogeneous background. It applies to broad classes of anisotropic and spatially varying electromagnetic media, including crystalline materials. The results therefore extend transformation-optics cloaking beyond idealized vacuum settings and place it on a rigorous operator-theoretic foundation. By combining singular transformation media, self-adjoint Maxwell dynamics, and time-dependent scattering theory, the paper proves that ideal transformation-optics cloaks make both passive and suitably compatible active objects electromagnetically invisible to all finite-energy exterior observations.
outputs.L5:
**There, The, and This**

The words **“there,” “the,”** and **“this”** are common in English, but they have different purposes. **“There”** can refer to a place or introduce the existence of something: “The book is over there” or “There is a book on the table.” **“The”** is used before a specific noun: “The book on the table is mine.” **“This”** points to a particular person, object, or idea that is close or currently being discussed: “This book is interesting.”

Together, they can form a simple sentence: **“There is the book—this is the one I wanted.”**

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft an academic abstract explaining how singular coordinate transformations, anisotropic transformation media, and the Schrödinger formulation of Maxwell’s equations yield an identity scattering operator and rigorous cloaking.
counterfactuals.output: **Abstract—** We present a rigorous framework for electromagnetic cloaking based on transformation optics. A singular coordinate transformation that blows up a point—or, more generally, a lower-dimensional set—into a finite cloaked region pushes forward the Euclidean permittivity and permeability tensors to anisotropic, spatially inhomogeneous, and singular transformation media. Because Maxwell’s equations are covariant under coordinate changes, electromagnetic fields in the exterior of the cloaked region are pullbacks of fields propagating in the untransformed background. Recasting the time-dependent Maxwell system in Schrödinger form, \(i\partial_t\Psi=H\Psi\), permits the transformed Maxwell operator to be defined as a self-adjoint operator on the appropriate finite-energy Hilbert space. The singular transformation then induces a unitary equivalence between the exterior dynamics and free-space evolution, while finite-energy conditions select the admissible self-adjoint realization and impose effective boundary conditions that decouple interior and exterior fields. Consequently, the exterior wave operators coincide with the transformation-induced identification, and the associated scattering operator is the identity: incident waves acquire neither a scattered far field nor externally detectable information about the cloaked contents. This operator-theoretic formulation converts the formal invariance argument of transformation optics into a rigorous statement of perfect cloaking, while clarifying the roles of anisotropy, material degeneracy, finite-energy solutions, and interior–exterior decoupling.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a paper that proves passive and active electromagnetic devices can be perfectly cloaked, including the roles of essential self-adjointness, unitary equivalence, and general anisotropic materials such as crystals.
counterfactuals.output:
The paper gives a rigorous operator-theoretic proof that an ideal transformation-optics cloak can completely isolate an electromagnetic region, whether that region contains only passive objects or active sources and devices.

### Core construction

A singular coordinate transformation “blows up” a point—or a set of points—into a finite cloaked region. Applying the transformation law for Maxwell’s equations produces anisotropic, spatially varying permittivity and permeability tensors that become singular or degenerate at the cloak’s inner boundary. Outside the cloak, fields are related to fields in the original, uncloaked space by the transformation.

### Essential self-adjointness

The authors formulate Maxwell evolution as an unbounded operator on the finite-energy Hilbert space. The Maxwell operator in the punctured virtual space is shown to be **essentially self-adjoint**: despite removing the points that are blown up, there is a unique physically meaningful self-adjoint extension.

This is important because self-adjointness provides:

- unique finite-energy electromagnetic evolution,
- conservation of energy,
- a mathematically unambiguous boundary behavior at the singular cloak interface.

The singular material tensors therefore do not require an arbitrary extra boundary condition on the exterior fields; the finite-energy condition selects the correct dynamics.

### Unitary equivalence

The coordinate transformation induces a **unitary map** between the electromagnetic energy space of the ordinary virtual medium and that of the cloaking medium. Under this map, the exterior Maxwell operator of the cloak is unitarily equivalent to the ordinary Maxwell operator in the punctured virtual space.

Consequently, exterior fields, scattering data, and boundary measurements are exactly those of the reference medium. An observer outside cannot distinguish the cloak and its contents from empty—or more generally prescribed—background space.

The total Maxwell operator separates into exterior and interior parts. This direct-sum structure means that:

- external fields do not enter the cloaked region;
- fields generated inside do not escape;
- passive objects inside produce no scattering;
- active currents or devices inside are also invisible to outside observers.

The interior dynamics may require its own self-adjoint boundary condition at the inner surface, but that choice does not affect exterior measurements.

### General anisotropic media

The argument is not restricted to isotropic vacuum. It begins with broad classes of positive anisotropic permittivity and permeability tensors and transports them through the singular transformation. Thus the reference medium and the cloaked contents may include anisotropic materials, including crystalline media. The proof depends on the operator and transformation structure rather than on scalar material parameters.

### Significance and limitations

The result establishes **perfect cloaking at the level of ideal finite-energy Maxwell theory**, including active devices, rather than merely approximate reduction of scattering. Its exactness relies on singular, strongly anisotropic constitutive tensors. Real metamaterials can only approximate these parameters and are constrained by loss, dispersion, bandwidth, fabrication errors, and source/interface compatibility, so physical implementations generally provide approximate rather than perfect cloaking.

counterfactuals.output: Electromagnetic invisibility cloaks seek to guide incident waves around a concealed region so that the exterior field is indistinguishable from propagation through empty space \cite{glu1, glu2, le}. In transformation-optics designs, this effect is achieved through spatially varying, anisotropic permittivity and permeability tensors derived from a singular coordinate transformation. Although ideal material parameters can suppress far-field scattering, their degeneracy at the cloaking interface introduces singular boundary behavior and raises subtle questions concerning finite-energy solutions, transmission conditions, and the physical interpretation of fields near the hidden boundary. A rigorous time-dependent scattering theory is therefore essential for determining how causal electromagnetic pulses interact with the cloak, whether transient signals reveal the concealed region, and under what assumptions perfect or approximate invisibility can be established.

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain rigorously why transformation-optics cloaks are invisible to electromagnetic waves when the coordinate map is the identity outside a ball, emphasizing that the exterior Maxwell propagator has a unique self-adjoint extension and that the scattering operator equals the identity.
counterfactuals.output:
Consider vacuum Maxwell equations on the virtual space \(\mathbb R^{3}\),

\[
\partial_t E=\varepsilon _0^{-1}\nabla\times H,\qquad
\partial_t H=-\mu _0^{-1}\nabla\times E.
\]

Let \(F:\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}\to \mathbb R^{3}\setminus\overline{B_a}\) be a smooth diffeomorphism that blows up the point \(0\) to the sphere \(\partial B_a\), and assume

\[
F(x)=x\qquad (|x|\ge R),\quad R>a.
\]

The cloak occupies \(B_R\setminus\overline{B_a}\). Its permittivity and permeability are the push-forwards of the vacuum tensors:

\[
\widetilde\varepsilon
  =\frac{DF\,\varepsilon_0\,DF^{T}}{|\det DF|}\circ F^{-1},
\qquad
\widetilde\mu
  =\frac{DF\,\mu_0\,DF^{T}}{|\det DF|}\circ F^{-1}.
\]

These tensors are singular at \(\partial B_a\); that singularity is essential to exact cloaking.

### 1. Maxwell dynamics is unitarily transformed vacuum dynamics

Put the vacuum fields in the energy Hilbert space

\[
\mathcal H_0=L^2_{\varepsilon_0}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)
\oplus L^2_{\mu_0}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3),
\]

with norm

\[
\|(E,H)\|_{\mathcal H_0}^2
=\int_{\mathbb R^3}
\big(E\cdot\varepsilon_0\overline E+
H\cdot\mu_0\overline H\big)\,dx.
\]

The vacuum Maxwell generator may be written, up to a conventional factor of \(i\), as

\[
A_0=
\begin{pmatrix}
0&i\varepsilon_0^{-1}\nabla\times\\
-i\mu_0^{-1}\nabla\times&0
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

On the physical, divergence-compatible finite-energy subspace, \(A_0\) is self-adjoint.

The pull-forward rule for electromagnetic one-forms defines a unitary map

\[
U_F:\mathcal H_0\longrightarrow \mathcal H_{\mathrm{ext}},
\]

where \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ext}}\) is the finite-energy space associated with
\((\widetilde\varepsilon,\widetilde\mu)\) in
\(\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline{B_a}\). In coordinates, the electric and magnetic covectors transform by

\[
\widetilde E(y)=DF(x)^{-T}E(x),\qquad
\widetilde H(y)=DF(x)^{-T}H(x),\qquad y=F(x).
\]

The constitutive push-forward formulas imply exact preservation of electromagnetic energy, hence unitarity. Covariance of curl then gives

\[
A_{\mathrm{ext}}=U_F A_0 U_F^{-1}.
\]

Thus the cloak exterior is not merely approximately equivalent to vacuum: its finite-energy Maxwell dynamics is exactly a unitary coordinate representation of vacuum dynamics.

### 2. Why the singular interface does not introduce extra exterior boundary data

Initially define the exterior Maxwell operator on smooth fields compactly supported away from the cloaking surface. Under \(U_F^{-1}\), this operator corresponds to the vacuum Maxwell operator defined on

\[
C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}).
\]

For finite-energy Maxwell fields in three dimensions, removing one point does not create a new self-adjoint boundary degree of freedom: the punctured-space Maxwell operator is essentially self-adjoint on the physical finite-energy subspace. Equivalently, its deficiency indices vanish. Therefore the transformed exterior operator has a unique self-adjoint extension,

\[
\overline{A_{\mathrm{ext}}}=U_F A_0 U_F^{-1}.
\]

This uniqueness is crucial. If several self-adjoint extensions were available, one could impose different boundary conditions at the singular surface, potentially producing different exterior fields and nontrivial scattering. Instead, finite energy and self-adjointness select one exterior evolution automatically.

The corresponding hidden boundary condition at \(\partial B_a\) is a consequence of the singular coefficients, not an independently prescribed reflecting boundary condition. It prevents energy flux across the cloaking surface. Consequently, the total Maxwell operator decomposes as

\[
A_{\mathrm{total}}
=A_{\mathrm{ext}}\oplus A_{\mathrm{int}},
\]

where \(A_{\mathrm{int}}\) is any chosen self-adjoint interior dynamics compatible with the model. Interior sources or eigenmodes cannot couple to the exterior finite-energy sector.

### 3. The exterior field is exactly the free field outside \(B_R\)

Because \(F\) is the identity for \(|x|\ge R\),

\[
U_F=I,\qquad
\widetilde\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0,\qquad
\widetilde\mu=\mu_0
\quad\text{for }|x|\ge R.
\]

If \(\Psi_0=(E_0,H_0)\) is a free Maxwell solution, the corresponding cloaking solution is

\[
\Psi(t)=U_F e^{-itA_0}\Psi_0.
\]

For \(|x|\ge R\), \(U_F\) acts as the identity, so

\[
\Psi(t,x)=e^{-itA_0}\Psi_0(x),\qquad |x|\ge R.
\]

Hence an observer outside \(B_R\) sees exactly the field that would be present in empty space. There is no scattered component.

The same argument applies in the frequency domain: away from exceptional issues associated only with the decoupled interior problem, every exterior finite-energy solution is the push-forward of a vacuum solution and agrees with it outside \(B_R\). Thus the exterior Cauchy data and boundary admittance maps coincide with those of vacuum.

### 4. The scattering operator is the identity

Let \(J\) be the natural identification of the free and cloaking energy spaces in the region where the coefficients agree. The wave operators are

\[
W_\pm
=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}
e^{itA_{\mathrm{ext}}}J e^{-itA_0}.
\]

Using \(A_{\mathrm{ext}}=U_FA_0U_F^{-1}\),

\[
e^{itA_{\mathrm{ext}}}
=U_F e^{itA_0}U_F^{-1}.
\]

Moreover, \(J-U_F\) is supported in the bounded region \(B_R\). Free Maxwell waves have local energy decay on the scattering subspace, so the contribution of \(J-U_F\) vanishes in the limits \(t\to\pm\infty\). Therefore

\[
W_+=W_-=U_F.
\]

The scattering operator is consequently

\[
S=W_+^*W_-=U_F^*U_F=I.
\]

Thus every incoming free state has exactly the same outgoing asymptotic state:

\[
\boxed{S=I.}
\]

In particular, the scattering amplitude and total scattering cross section vanish at every frequency for which the finite-energy exterior scattering problem is defined. Exact invisibility follows from three facts together: transformation covariance of Maxwell’s equations, uniqueness of the self-adjoint exterior propagator, and the coordinate map being exactly the identity outside a bounded region.
